answers.ask: Should the court sit in a stadium with seating, or on an open bright backdrop with nothing around it?
answers.answer: Use an open bright backdrop with nothing around the court; keep the first build focused on the playable tennis space rather than stadium scenery.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D arcade tennis map centered on a single standard singles court, with clear boundary lines, service boxes, a central net, and open run-off space around all sides. Use a bright, empty backdrop with no stadium seating or surrounding scenery, keeping the court as the sole focal point. Compose the view from an elevated third-person broadcast angle behind one baseline, showing both player positions across the net and most of the full court.
agent_notes: Singles tennis with standard scoring on a marked court is Sports, and space-bounded is the genre default for exactly this: baselines and sidelines as a rigid perimeter with play contained inside. Court Sport is the matching preset — out detection is trigger-bounds, the in-court landing halves are the scoring planes, and the serve boxes are the play-start positions. The answer rules out a stadium, so I dropped all the dressing options and left the court on an open bright backdrop, which keeps the whole build on P0 with no tiered seating. The net is real geometry with no option row of its own; it rides along as a detail, and the court itself is a regulation template better placed parametrically than drawn, which is a generator choice rather than a routing one.
